data.title: Browser DevTools
data.tagline: Browser DevTools are built-in tools for inspecting page structure, styles, errors, requests, and storage state.
data.learningOutcome: You can choose Elements, Console, Network, or Storage from the visible symptom, record evidence, and describe the issue to an AI Agent.
data.description: For example, when Save does not update the page, use Elements for nodes and styles, Console for script errors, Network for request status and responses, and Storage for browser data such as cookies. DevTools provides evidence and temporary edits; it does not replace server logs, permission checks, or a real code fix.

learning.assumes: You have opened a web page and encountered a display problem, an unresponsive action, or a failed request.
learning.outcome: You can choose Elements, Console, Network, or Storage from the visible symptom, record evidence, and describe the issue to an AI Agent.

distinctions.label: Terminal
distinctions.explanation: Browser DevTools inspects a page from inside the browser; Terminal runs commands and tools in the development environment.

distinctions.label: Server log
distinctions.explanation: Browser DevTools shows what the browser can observe; Server Logs records events inside the server and can explain failures the browser cannot see.

explanation.title: How to open DevTools
explanation.text: Right-click and select 'Inspect' or 'Inspect Element'. Shortcuts: Mac Cmd+Option+I, Windows F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I. Opens to Elements panel by default, click tabs to switch to Console, Network, or Application.

explanation.title: Elements and Console
explanation.text: Elements inspects the current DOM, attributes, and CSS; Console shows script errors, logs, and reproducible runtime information.

explanation.title: Network and Storage
explanation.text: Network inspects requests, status codes, request data, and responses; Storage inspects browser state such as cookies and Web Storage. Choose by symptom, then carry evidence into the fix and retest.

data.boundary: DevTools is for observing and locating problems, not an automatic repair button. It cannot replace server logs, database records, or backend authorization checks; a temporary edit in a panel is not a change to the project files.

lessonPractice.title: Clicking Save does not update the page, and the server response is needed to explain the failure. Which panel should you open first?

options.label: Open Network and inspect the save request's status, payload, and response
options.feedback: Correct. The server status and response are network evidence, and Network shows where the save flow stopped.

options.label: Open Elements and keep changing the button text until it looks saved
options.feedback: Elements is for nodes and styles. Changing text cannot prove the request succeeded or reveal the server's reason.

options.label: Open Storage, delete all browser data, and click Save again
options.feedback: Clearing storage may lose a session or draft without explaining this failure. Preserve and inspect the request evidence first.

data.agentPrompt: Use the browser developer tools to investigate the failed save. State what you found in Elements, Console, Network, or Storage, especially the save request's status and response. Modify the code only after finding evidence, then send the request again and confirm the page updates.
